My advice is to follow a regular maintenance schedule, make sure to replace worn parts before they break to avoid damaging other parts, and overall love the car. If you fall in love and show that love, it'll last you over 200K

Follow the maintenance schedule.

Check your fluids regularly.

Wash your car, and splurge for the under body flush.

If you get a ding/chip, get cover-up paint on it immediately.

Learn the noises your car makes. New noises are rarely good. It's a warning, not an oddity to be ignored.

Change your brake pads before the rotors are destroyed, or at least before the calipers are.

Change your oxygen sensors every 5 years. They don't last as long as they're supposed to.

Get a code reader, or a friend with a code reader. That light might be something stupid you can fix cheaply and immediately yourself. Instead of dreading, and putting off a potentially expensive trip to the shop.

Don't use the cheapest oil or filter you can find.

Run some injector cleaner through the car before you think you need it.

Cheap wiper blades suck. Get Bosch icons. They cost a third more, but last twice as long, and do a way better job.
If you're comfortable doing this (I don't know handy you are), put anti-seize on every suspension, subframe, and exhaust bolt you can find. You'll thank me in ten years.

If you have to take a belt off for any reason, replace it. Same goes for things like the water pump. It's a bitch to get at, and its cheap. If you're in there anyhow, just replace it.

Never reuse a gasket. Seriously, just don't.
Subaru recommends that customers treat the first oil change as their second. So, do your first at 3 months or 3,000 miles and the second at 6 months or six thousand miles.
